prose.text: {{sandbox-activity-what}} {{sandbox-activity-weeks}} {{sandbox-activity-reading}} The API detail report by MD5 is covered in [[zia.sandbox.report]].

prose.label: Weekly emails.
prose.text: {{sandbox-weekly-email}} {{sffm-weekly-email}} The link validity of Interactive Reports schedules is in [[zia.reports.interactive:schedule-links]]. checks.do: Whether the organization has Advanced Sandbox before expecting the Sandbox Files Found Malicious Report.
Whether a known malicious file shown as allowed is explained by a missing Advanced Sandbox or Sandbox rule, or by the Allow & Scan action.

cyber-insights-what.statement: Cybersecurity Insights provides unified real-time visibility into critical security incidents and policy actions, to understand the security efficacy of layered defense across Malware Protection, Advanced Threat Protection (ATP), Sandbox, Firewall and Zero Trust Browser (formerly Isolation).

quotes: Cybersecurity Insights provides a unified real-time visibility into critical security incidents and policy actions to understand the security efficacy of layered defense across Malware Protection, Advanced Threat Protection (ATP), Sandbox, Firewall, and Zero Trust Browser (formerly Isolation) for your organization.

cyber-insights-time.statement: Cybersecurity Insights can be filtered to the last 1 hour, 4 hours, 1 day, 7 days or 14 days; the default is the last 1 hour.

quotes: Filter to view data for the last 1 hour, 4 hours, 1 day, 7 days, or 14 days. The default time is the last 1 hour.

cyber-insights-unknown.statement: Its threat categories include Sandbox Offensive Security Tools, Sandbox Ransomware, Crypto Mining and Domain Generated Algorithm Domains, and Unknown represents all the incidents the Zscaler service was unable to classify under a threat category.

quotes: - Sandbox Offensive Security Tools
- Sandbox Ransomware
- Crypto Mining
- Domain Generated Algorithm Domains
Unknown (this represents all the incidents that the Zscaler service was unable to classify under a threat category or were not classifiable under any of the preceding categories)

cyber-insights-top10.statement: Top Locations, Top Users, Top Departments and Top AI/ML Detection Source by Security Incidents each show the top 10.

quotes: Top Locations by Security Incidents: View the top 10 locations with incidents
Top Users by Security Incidents: View the top 10 users with incidents
Top Departments by Security Incidents: View the top 10 departments with incidents
Top AI/ML Detection Source by Incidents: View the top 10 AI/ML detection sources with incidents

cyber-insights-incident-detail.statement: An incident's details include the Sandbox Category (if the file is sent for sandbox analysis) and the MD5 hash of the file that triggered the rule; Impacted Systems lists each client's Client External IP (the internet gateway location IP address) and the number of related allowed transactions.

quotes: Sandbox Category: The name of the sandbox category, if the file is sent for sandbox analysis.
MD5: The MD5 hash for the file that triggered the rule.
Client External IP: The internet gateway location IP address of the client.
Allowed Transactions: The number of user transactions that were allowed related to the incident.

cyber-insights-pdf.statement: The latest Zscaler ThreatLabz updates can be downloaded as a PDF file with Save as PDF.

quotes: To download the latest Zscaler ThreatLabz updates as a PDF file, click Save as PDF.

sandbox-activity-what.statement: The Sandbox Activity Report highlights the Sandbox policy action taken for known and unknown files. Unknown files are files the sandbox encounters for the first time; files known by cloud effect are files from any organization that the sandbox analyzed and classified as malicious or benign.

quotes: The Sandbox Activity Report highlights the Sandbox policy action taken for known and unknown files in your organization.
Unknown files are files that the sandbox encounters for the first time. Files known by cloud effect are files from any organization that the sandbox analyzed and classified as malicious or benign.

sandbox-activity-weeks.statement: The Sandbox Activity Report shows weekly reports from the last 6 months, not including the current week; Transactions include all download attempts, even of the same file, while Unique Files count each file once. The displayed transactions export to a PDF or JSON file.

quotes: You can view weekly reports from the last 6 months, not including the current week.
Transactions include all download attempts, even of the same file. Unique Files count each file once, regardless of the number of transactions.
Export the displayed transactions to a PDF or JSON file.

sandbox-activity-reading.statement: Known malicious files might have been allowed because the organization does not have Advanced Sandbox or the correct Sandbox rule configured. A quarantined file could also be counted under Allow & Scan if it was allowed while in quarantine. Malicious files downloaded due to the Allow & Scan policy action are patient 0 events.

quotes: Known malicious files might have been allowed because you don't have Advanced Sandbox or the correct Sandbox rule configured.
A situation might occur where a file that has been quarantined could also be counted under Allow & Scan if the file was allowed while in quarantine.
Malicious files downloaded due to the Allow & Scan policy action are patient 0 events.

sffm-needs-advanced.statement: Advanced Sandbox is required to view the Sandbox Files Found Malicious Report, which highlights unknown files sent to the sandbox for analysis and found to be malicious; it shows weekly reports from the last 6 months, not including the current week, and the displayed transactions export to a PDF or CSV file.

quotes: You must have Advanced Sandbox to view the Sandbox Files Found Malicious Report.
highlights unknown files that were sent to the sandbox for analysis and found to be malicious.
You can view weekly reports from the last 6 months, not including the current week.
Export the displayed transactions to a PDF or CSV file.

sffm-columns.statement: Per file the report shows the MD5 of a file the organization saw for the first time (click it to view the Sandbox Detail Report), the Allowed Transactions before the file was found malicious (patient 0 events) and the Blocked Transactions after.

quotes: MD5: The MD5 of a file that your organization has seen for the first time. Click to view the Sandbox Detail Report.
Allowed Transactions: The number of allowed transactions for the file before the file was found to be malicious. These transactions are patient 0 events.
Blocked Transactions: The number of blocked transactions for the file after the file was found to be malicious.

sandbox-weekly-email.statement: The Zscaler service can email recipients a preview of the Sandbox Activity Report and a link to the full report, a static page where recipients can view and print it. Anyone who has the link can access the report. Frequency is weekly and cannot be modified; the administrator chooses the Day and the Time Zone the service uses when it generates the report.

quotes: The Zscaler service can directly email your recipients a preview of the Sandbox Activity Report and a link to the full report. The full report is a static page where recipients can view and print the report.
Anyone who has the link can access the report.
Frequency: The Zscaler service emails the report weekly to your added recipients. You can't modify this field.
Day: Choose which day the Zscaler service emails the report.
Time Zone: Choose the time zone that the Zscaler service uses when it generates the report.

sffm-weekly-email.statement: The Zscaler service can email recipients a preview of the Sandbox Files Found Malicious Report and a link to the full report. Anyone who has the link can access the report. Frequency is weekly and cannot be modified; the administrator chooses the Day.

quotes: The Zscaler service can directly email your recipients a preview of the Sandbox Files Found Malicious Report and a link to the full report.
Anyone who has the link can access the report.
Frequency: The Zscaler service emails the report weekly to your added recipients. You can't modify this field.
Day: Choose which day the Zscaler service emails the report.

sffm-email-path.summary: The scheduling page for the Sandbox Files Found Malicious weekly email gives a click path to the Instance Discovery Report, while the report's own page places it under the Sandbox Activity Report.

quotes: From the navigation menu, go to Analytics > Reports > Instance Discovery Report.

positions.says: Step 1 of the SFFM scheduling procedure goes to Analytics > Reports > Instance Discovery Report.

quotes: (Analytics > Reports > Sandbox Activity Report > Sandbox Files Found Malicious)

positions.says: The report is at Analytics > Reports > Sandbox Activity Report > Sandbox Files Found Malicious.

sffm-email-path.impact: The scheduling procedure's first step names a different report page than the one that holds the SFFM report.

cyber-retention.title: Cybersecurity Insights retention beyond the 14-day filter
cyber-retention.detail: The page lists time filters up to the last 14 days and does not say how long incident data is kept.

week-and-freeze.title: Sandbox report week time zone and whether the emailed static report freezes at send time
week-and-freeze.detail: The Sandbox report pages show weekly reports without naming the time zone that defines a week. The email pages call the full report a static page, but do not say whether its data is fixed at the time of sending.
